name: epsilon
why: A wavelet image compressor is a window into transform math, and it is obscure enough to be a genuine find.

brief.what_it_is: EPSILON is an open source command-line wavelet image compressor, according to its SourceForge page. The page says it is aimed at parallel and robust image processing. The page gives no input or output formats and no usage details. The brew metadata lists three executables: epsilon, start_epsilon_nodes.pl, and stop_epsilon_nodes.pl. The two Perl scripts suggest a multi-node setup, but the page does not confirm that.
brief.why_it_exists: The page gives only the one-line description: an open source wavelet image compressor aimed at parallel and robust image processing. It gives no further problem statement.
brief.install_notes: The SourceForge page lists operating systems as BSD, Linux, and Windows, with C and Perl as the programming languages and a command-line interface. No build steps, dependencies, or first-run instructions appeared on the page. The Perl node scripts imply a multi-machine setup, but I did not see how to configure it.
brief.standout: Wavelet compression is a less common niche than JPEG or PNG tooling, and the project pairs it with parallel processing and node start/stop scripts. Those scripts are only visible in the brew metadata, not on the page.
brief.status: Quiet. The SourceForge page shows a last update of 2014-06-17 and a registration date of 2006-10-02. It reports 21 downloads this week. I saw no newer release or commit information.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a SourceForge landing page with no README, documentation, or usage examples, so I could not verify how the tool is driven or what its output looks like. The entry should not describe features beyond the one-line summary. The project's own web site is linked from the page, but I did not have its URL and did not fetch it. The last recorded update is about a decade old, so builds may be hard to reproduce on current systems. The brew caveats field was empty.
quotes: EPSILON is a powerful Open Source wavelet image compressor. The project is aimed on parallel and robust image processing.
fetch_log: https://sourceforge.net/projects/epsilon-project/ — fetched OK, but it is a SourceForge landing page with no README. It contains the description, license (GPLv2 / LGPLv2), platforms, languages, and last-update date. I did not follow the linked 'EPSILON Web Site', whose URL did not appear in the text I received.
